newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurdish group says ceasefire holding.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish group says ceasefire holding.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish faction said on Thursday a U.S.-brokered ceasefire to end two months of inter-Kurdish fighting in northern Iraq was holding.

"Hopefully, it is holding. We are watching the situation now. We have not got any more reports of fighting after midnight," said Faik Nerweyi, Ankara spokesman for the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).
The KDP and rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) pledged to observe a ceasefire from midnight Iraqi time (2000 GMT on Wednesday), the U.S. State Department said.

"There were orders to that effect on the ground yesterday because we were expecting this, but we haven't been in contact with Iraqi Kurdistan this morning," said Shazad Saib, the PUK's Turkey's representative.

U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau got an agreement to halt the fighting from the two factions' leaders at separate meetings in Turkey this week. The clashes damaged U.S. interests in northern Iraq and threatened to draw in Iraq and Iran.
Iraqi troops and tanks helped the KDP capture the city of Arbil from the PUK on August 31, prompting retaliatory U.S. missile strikes against Iraqi military targets.
